description:
Build one harness that measures the four cost claims of this epic against a pinned pre-change binary and any tip binary, with ratio thresholds computed within one run, record that the base reproduces each cost, and record the tip run once the four reductions have landed (`@/charter/D-17`, `@/charter/D-19`).

## Background

- The claims (REQ-22): bulk update at a fixed match count grows with matches times repository issues because `transition_blockers` lists every issue per matched state change (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3258-3288`, called from `crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs:480`); archive candidates re-read configuration, issues and the event log per candidate (`archive_candidates`, `crates/jit/src/commands/archive.rs:158-170`, planning each candidate through `plan_archive_target` at `:184`; measured at 87 s for 190 candidates); one mutation parses its declarations more than once (`dep add` at `crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:384-385`, `issue delete` once more at `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:75-76`; investigation configuration C5 lists the rest); redo apply walks each parent chain three times per operation (`apply_operations`, `crates/jit/src/storage/redo_apply.rs:130-176`, and `resolve`, `:196-205`).
- Conventions: `dev/benchmarks/publication-cost-722878d4/README.md` (named base commit built in a detached worktree, binary hashes, load wait) and `dev/benchmarks/nextest-concurrency-934985ca/` (`validate.py` rederives the verdict). Issue-bound benchmark directories end in the issue's short id.
- The base commit is `369d35a42`.
- The four reductions the tip run measures: bulk applies in one session (`bulk-apply-one-session`), candidates plan in one session (`archive-candidates-one-session`), a mutation parses declarations once per captured image (`declarations-on-mutation-base`), and redo apply opens each parent once with syncs as REQ-15 settled them (`redo-apply-parents-once`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `scripts/benchmark-cost-evidence.sh <tip-binary>` builds the base from `369d35a42`, fails with an install hint when `strace` is absent, and runs four scenarios on both binaries in one run: (a) bulk `--state in_progress` over M ∈ {10, 40} matches in repositories of N ∈ {500, 2000} issues, reporting the per-match slope s(N) = (t(M=40) − t(M=10))/30; (b) `jit archive candidates --json` over C ∈ {10, 40} terminal containers, reporting the per-candidate slope and the `openat` count of `config.toml`; (c) `jit dep add` over minimal and inflated declarations (2,000 namespace values, 300 rules), reporting the declaration-attributable time D = t(inflated) − t(minimal); (d) `jit profile add` of a fixed 48-file package over four nested directories, reporting directory `openat` and `fsync` counts.
- [hard] REQ-02: The pass thresholds, computed per run as medians of five samples: (a) tip s(2000)/s(500) ≤ 1.5; (b) tip per-candidate slope ≤ 0.5 × base and tip `config.toml` opens equal at C = 10 and C = 40; (c) tip D ≤ 0.7 × base D; (d) tip directory opens ≤ 0.6 × base, with fsync counts recorded.
- [hard] REQ-03: A base-only run is recorded under `dev/benchmarks/cost-evidence-<short-id>/raw/base/`, where `<short-id>` is this issue's short id, and the README shows the base reproduces each cost: s(2000)/s(500) ≥ 2.5, `config.toml` opens grow with C, and D > 0.
- [hard] REQ-04: `dev/benchmarks/cost-evidence-<short-id>/raw/tip/` holds one harness run of base and tip over the finished tip, with binary hashes and host load, and `summary.json` records each scenario's ratios and verdict.
- [hard] REQ-05: `validate.py` rederives every ratio and verdict from `raw/`, all four verdicts pass, and the README states the directory-sync outcome REQ-15 reached.

## Notes

- A failing tip verdict is reported to the lead with its numbers; the harness thresholds are not changed in this task.
- The tip run happens once the four reductions have landed; the base record is taken first.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Cost evidence: the epic's four cost reductions against the base binary
